Two screens, one iPhone—Apple just rewrote the form factor.

The iPhone Duo’s hinge design means we’ll finally have native multitasking without resorting to split‑view hacks. For developers, that’s a call to rethink UI layouts, state management, and how we surface AI‑driven features across two displays. It also forces us to consider power budgeting: a second screen doubles the graphics pipeline, so efficiency becomes a first‑class concern.

I’m curious how quickly the SDK will expose dual‑screen primitives and whether Apple will provide guidelines for adaptive design. Will we see a wave of apps that treat the two panels as a single canvas, or will most developers stick to mirrored experiences?

How are you planning to adapt your next project for a dual‑screen iPhone?
